title: Mesh nebulizer price in Pakistan: how mesh models work and what to check

description: Mesh nebulizer price in Pakistan explained: how vibrating mesh models work, how they compare with compressor units, specs to check and running costs.
answer: The price of a mesh nebulizer in Pakistan depends on the brand, mesh design, power options, accessories and the rupee exchange rate on the day of import, so there is no single fixed price. body:
A mesh nebulizer is a small electronic device that turns liquid medicine into a fine mist using a vibrating plate full of tiny holes. Many buyers in Pakistan ask for one because it is quiet and light. This guide explains how mesh models work, how they differ from compressor models, what changes the price and what to check before you order. It is a buying guide only. Which medicine you use, and how much, is for your doctor to decide.

What is a mesh nebulizer and how does it work?

A mesh nebulizer makes a mist by forcing liquid medicine through a metal plate (the mesh) that vibrates and is drilled with very small holes. A piezoelectric element, a part that moves when electricity is applied, drives the vibration. No compressed air is needed, which is why these units are small and quiet.

There are two main designs:

  • Active mesh: the mesh plate itself vibrates. This design can nebulize very small volumes.
  • Passive mesh: the mesh stays still and a vibrating horn behind the liquid pushes it through the holes.

Typical droplet sizes for mesh devices are about 2 to 6 microns (MMAD, mass median aerodynamic diameter). PARI, a German nebulizer maker, explains that particles under 5 microns are the ones that reach the lungs, while larger ones settle in the throat and windpipe.

How is a mesh nebulizer different from a compressor nebulizer?

The main difference is the power source of the mist: a compressor nebulizer uses a pump that blows air through a jet, while a mesh nebulizer uses a vibrating plate. That changes the size, noise level and running parts. The table below compares published figures for three branded models, as listed on the makers' websites at the time of writing (November 2026).

Compressor units are known for being durable and simple. Mesh units leave less medicine behind in the cup. A respiratory therapy reference puts the leftover (residual) volume at about 0.1 to 0.4 mL for a vibrating mesh device, against about 0.8 to 1.5 mL for many other liquid nebulizers. Omron also lists 360 degree operation for the NE-U100, meaning it is designed to work in any position.

What changes the price of a mesh nebulizer in Pakistan?

The price of a mesh nebulizer in Pakistan changes mainly with the brand, the mesh design and what comes in the box. There is no single fixed rate, because almost all units are imported and priced on the day of order. The main factors are:

  • Brand and model: branded mesh units from makers such as Omron and PARI usually cost more than generic handheld models. PARI notes that mesh membranes are expensive to make.
  • Mesh type: active and passive designs differ in build and in which liquids they handle.
  • Power options: some models include an AC adapter, others sell it separately. Rechargeable models carry a built-in battery.
  • Accessories: adult and child masks, mouthpieces, spare medicine cups and storage cases change the total.
  • Spare parts: replacement mesh caps or yearly part packs add to the long-term cost.
  • Exchange rate and import costs: the rupee rate, freight and duties on the day of import all feed into the final price. Duty and tax rules change, so check the current rule.
  • Quantity: a clinic ordering several units may get a different unit price from a single buyer.

For these reasons SurgiSource does not publish a fixed price. You can see the general nebulizer price page and then ask for today's quote.

What specifications should you check before buying?

Check the particle size, the output rate, the power options and the cup size before you compare prices. These numbers are printed in the instruction manual or on the maker's product page.

  • Particle size (MMAD or MMD): the figure tells you the typical droplet size. Compare models using the same unit.
  • Output rate: PARI lists 497 mg per minute for the VELOX, measured with 2.5 mL of 0.9 percent saline. When you compare models, make sure the rates were measured the same way.
  • Power: note the battery type, how long a set lasts and whether a mains adapter is included.
  • Sound level: quoted in dBA. Omron lists under 23 dBA for its mesh unit and about 52 dBA for its tabletop compressor.
  • Warranty: Omron's US page lists 2 years for the NE-U100 main unit, with accessories and batteries excluded. Ask what the warranty covers in Pakistan for the unit you buy.
  • Masks and mouthpieces: check that the sizes you need come in the box.

How do you look after the mesh, and what are the running costs?

The mesh must be kept clean and never scrubbed or touched, because dried medicine can block the tiny holes and weaken the mist. A blocked mesh can lead to longer sessions or a unit that stops working.

Makers handle this in different ways. PARI sells a cleaning aid called VELOXcare that rinses and clears the membrane pores, and offers a yearly pack of replacement parts. Some mesh parts cannot be washed in the usual way and some mesh plates have a limited life. Ask for the cleaning instructions and the price of spare parts before you buy, as these are part of the real cost. Our guide on how to clean a nebulizer covers general care.

Can every nebulized medicine be used in a mesh nebulizer?

No, not every medicine is suitable for every mesh device, and some medicines are approved only for use with one specific nebulizer. This is a medical decision. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether the medicine you have been prescribed can be used in the model you plan to buy, and follow your doctor's advice on dose and timing.

Because mesh devices waste less medicine in the cup, the amount reaching the patient can be higher than with an older device. That is another reason to tell your doctor if you change from a compressor to a mesh nebulizer.

Is a mesh nebulizer regulated as a medical device in Pakistan?

Yes, a nebulizer is made for treatment, and the medical device definition used by the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) covers products made for diagnosis or treatment. DRAP sorts medical devices into four risk classes, A (low hazard) to D (high hazard), and publishes lists of establishment licences issued under the Medical Devices Rules 2017.

DRAP's public risk classification page gives examples for each class but does not name nebulizers, so check the current DRAP listing for the exact product if you need its class. In the United States, Omron's page notes that federal law restricts sale of the NE-U100 to the order of a licensed practitioner. Rules differ by country, so follow your doctor's advice and check the current rule in Pakistan.

faqs: What is the price of a mesh nebulizer in Pakistan?

There is no fixed price because mesh nebulizers are imported and priced on the day of order. The brand, accessories, spare parts, quantity and the rupee exchange rate all change the total. SurgiSource quotes today's price in rupees through its quote form.
Is a mesh nebulizer better than a compressor nebulizer?

Neither is better for everyone. Mesh units are smaller, quieter and leave less medicine in the cup, while compressor units are simple and durable. Your doctor can advise which suits the prescribed medicine.
Can a mesh nebulizer run on batteries?
Many can. Omron's MicroAir NE-U100 runs on AA batteries or an AC adapter, and the PARI VELOX runs on three AA batteries or a mains adapter.
Why does a mesh nebulizer stop producing mist?
The most common cause is dried medicine blocking the tiny holes in the mesh. Follow the maker's cleaning steps after each use and never scrub or touch the mesh.
Do I need a prescription to buy a mesh nebulizer in Pakistan?
Rules differ by country and change over time, so check the current DRAP rule. The medicine used in the nebulizer should always be prescribed by your doctor.
